title: Kashmir Schools Reopen After Extended Summer Break - The Chenab Times
full_text:
SRINAGAR: Educational institutions across the Kashmir Valley resumed operations on Monday, marking the end of an extended summer vacation. The reopening followed an unusual period of closures initially prompted by a severe heatwave and subsequently prolonged by heavy rainfall and flood-like conditions.
Schools Welcome Students Back After Unforeseen Holidays
Information was available with The Chenab Times indicating that students, clad in their school uniforms, began reporting to their respective institutions early Monday morning. The resumption of academic activities signals a return to normalcy for students and educators alike after the extended break.
The initial closure of schools was scheduled for July 6, lasting for 13 days, as the valley grappled with a significantly hotter than usual summer. This period of intense heat put a strain on daily life and educational continuity.
However, the anticipated end to the summer heat arrived not with clear skies but with substantial rainfall around July 18. The subsequent downpour led to a flood-like situation in several areas, prompting the administration to extend the holidays further, pushing the reopening date to July 26.
This extended closure meant that students missed nearly three weeks of regular schooling. The decision to extend the holidays was primarily a precautionary measure to ensure the safety of students and staff amidst the adverse weather conditions and the resulting disruptions.
The administration closely monitored the situation following the heavy rains. As the water levels receded and the immediate threat of flooding subsided, authorities assessed the safety and accessibility of school premises. This careful evaluation paved the way for the decision to reopen schools on Monday.
The reopening is expected to allow academic sessions to resume their intended pace. Educators will now focus on catching up on any missed curriculum and ensuring a smooth transition back into the regular academic routine. The experience has highlighted the impact of extreme weather events on educational infrastructure and scheduling in the region.
